fixes.explanation: Sealing it shut isn't in this psalm, friend. Asaph, the psalm's writer, says the nations "…have defiled Your holy temple…" That's the word he uses, and he says it straight to God. The temple was defiled.

Guards aren't mentioned in this verse, friend. Asaph, the psalm's writer, says the nations "…have invaded Your inheritance; they have defiled Your holy temple…" Invaded and defiled are his words. He says them straight to God.

Slowly isn't what Asaph asks for, friend. He says, "let Your compassion come quickly, for we are brought low." The reason sits right there in the verse. Being brought low is why he wants God's compassion now.
Eventually isn't in the verse, friend. Asaph says, "let Your compassion come quickly…" Quickly, not someday. The people are brought low, and he says so.

Yes, friend. Asaph asks why the nations should ask, "Where is their God?" (Ps 79:10) He doesn't want that question asked. Then he asks God to make known among the nations His vengeance for the bloodshed of His servants.
That question isn't in the psalm, friend. Asaph asks why the nations should ask, "Where is their God?" (Ps 79:10) The question is about God, not a king. It's the one he doesn't want asked.

Fighting back never comes up in these verses, friend. Asaph asks why the nations should ask, "Where is their God?" (Ps 79:10) I think that question worries him. It's about God, and he puts it right into his prayer.

The groans in this verse belong to the captives, friend, not the nations. Asaph prays, "May the groans of the captives reach You…" (Ps 79:11) The nations are the invaders in this psalm. The word that fits is captives.

Neighbors do show up in this psalm, friend, but the groans belong to the captives. Asaph prays, "May the groans of the captives reach You…" (Ps 79:11) He's praying for people who are held. Captives is the word.

False is right, friend. Asaph says, "…we Your people, the sheep of Your pasture, will thank You forever…" (Ps 79:13) Forever, not once. Then he adds, "from generation to generation we will declare Your praise."
